claim: Google is testing whether AI compute can be hosted in orbit, using a prototype satellite and laser interconnect concepts.
verifiedFacts: Google plans a prototype satellite launch on October 1 for Project Suncatcher.
The experiment uses Trillium TPUs and tests radiation, cooling and solar-power assumptions.
The long-term concept includes satellite constellations and laser-based interconnectivity.
inference: This is a frontier infrastructure signal about energy, cooling and geography of compute, not a near-term product opportunity.

Consultancy implication: preserve as a surprise architecture reference for infrastructure scenarios; do not spin out a space-compute workstream. Project disposition: Seed Loom REFERENCE-ONLY; Omni-Loom REFERENCE-ONLY for physical-system provenance parallels.
significance: Medium-high: it reframes AI infrastructure as an energy/physics problem with strong systems-engineering implications.
assumptions: The prototype mission occurs as reported and yields useful engineering data.
knownLimitations: Early experiment; feasibility and economics remain highly uncertain.
